newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Union Miniere share rises to key level.
newsitem.headline: Union Miniere share rises to key level.

text.p: Shares in Belgian non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere are close to a 12-month high, forging ahead on optimism about zinc prices, the dollar and the supply situation in the zinc market, analysts said Monday.
The stock closed on Monday at 2,400 francs, up 0.8 percent, and outperforming the Bel-20 share index which ended at 2,053.51 points, up only 0.01 percent.

Its year high of 2,440 francs was recorded on April 26, 1996 and seen again on July 1 after a double correction. Subsequent buying and selling waves took the stock to a high of 2,410 on September 20 and a low of 2,100 on January 2, 1997.
Since the start of the year it has mostly been go for the share, producing a gain of 14 percent over the past month. By comparison the Bel-20 gained just under 10 percent.
Monday's gain came on the back of news that Australian miner MIM Holdings Ltd told European smelters it would cut supplies of zinc concentrates by half this year.
A tighter market and higher prices should be the result, analysts said.
In London zinc prices were probing Friday's highs of $1,174 in the wake of MIM news.

Metal Bulletin research said in a report on Monday that growth in western world zinc consumption would resume in 1997, kicking off several years of expansion. Prices would peak at over $1,650 basis LME cash in 1998.
UM activities involving zinc include refining and sheets for the building industry.
"Zinc prices are looking very good," said broker Damien Crispiels at Bank Degroof in Brussels, who also pointed to the dollar's strength.

Already in the first half of 1996 exchange rate gains helped limit the pressure on earnings from declining or merely stable metal prices. Nevertheless, group net profit was down 10 percent at 281 million francs, while current profit fell by 30 percent.
At the time of reporting the six months results, Union Miniere forecast that, all things being equal, second half results would exceed those of the first half.
UM made group net loss of 954 million francs in 1995, but a current profit of 1.8 billion, the difference being mainly the result of restructuring costs.

Degroof's Crispiels noted that UM's shares were also being underpinned by the fact that industry zinc stocks currently were enough for only 2.5 weeks consumption. "This is very low," he said. Normally, stocks covered six to 12 weeks.
"2,400 is an important level for the share," he said.
A break above could clear the way for new year highs, analysts said.

The company is due to publish full year 1996 earnings on March 13. Analysts forecast 1996 earnings per share of 60-80 francs and see EPS doubling to 118-140 francs in 1997. EPS rose to 63 francs in 1995 from 27 in 1994.
